upstream: sherpa-onnx KWS zipformer2 zh-en 3M (k2-fsa), release archive sherpa-onnx-kws-zipformer-zh-en-3M-2025-12-20.tar.bz2 (GitHub release tag kws-models), encoder/decoder/joiner-epoch-13-avg-2-chunk-8-left-64.onnx

artefacts.kws_zipformer_zh_en_3m_decoder_joiner.np: decoder + joiner weights, float32 [2V+2D, D+1] = [1166, 321], V = 263, D = 320; row layout in export.py decoder_joiner_table (CPU)

input_shape: 39 inputs: x 1x29x80, pad_mask 1x72, 37 caches (cached_key/nonlin_attn/val1/val2/conv1/conv2 x 6 stacks, embed_states 1x128x3x19)
input_note: All featuremap / no_preprocess. x = 80-bin kaldi fbank (samples in [-1, 1], Povey window, low_freq 20, high_freq -400, dither 0, snip_edges=false), 29 frames per call advancing by 16 (160 ms). pad_mask = [1]*(64-q) + [0]*(q+8), q = min(processed, 64), processed += 8 per call (the EMBEDDING rate, not the 4 encoder frames out). Caches start at zero and are fed back from the matching new_<name> output.

outputs.encoder_out: 1x4x320, four 40 ms frames already in the joiner's space (encoder_proj is inside the graph)

licence.tier: UNRESOLVED — recipe only, do not redistribute the .hbm yet
licence.detail: sherpa-onnx (code, export scripts, the keyword search this build reproduces) is Apache-2.0. The model is published by the k2-fsa project as a GitHub release asset (tag kws-models) with no model-specific licence, and the release does not say what the zh-en model was trained on. Its Chinese-only sibling is trained on WenetSpeech; whether that, or which English corpus, is in the zh-en model is not stated. Silence is not permission: the recipe is public, the binary is not. The same rewrites should carry over to a zipformer2 streaming KWS model trained on data you can account for, though only this one has been run.
licence.link_in_chain: weights (no licence attached to the release asset) and training data (undisclosed)

toolchain.note: Compiled through hbc.py: plain hb_compile segfaults (container exit 139) right after 'Start to optimize the onnx model.' because one hmct optimiser check builds an onnxruntime session that crashes on this graph.

C.on: one AISHELL-1 utterance, BCDL on the board, shipped build

cosine.note: Below the repo's usual 0.99 gate, and not a failure. A is the compiler's own encoder_out cosine for the shipped build (quantized model vs float, on the calibration set; 0.948916 for the rebuild). C is the on-board encoder_out against float on one AISHELL-1 utterance: per 40 ms frame 0.995 mean, 0.973 worst; over the whole array 0.915, because some frames come out smaller rather than turned, which the joiner's tanh and the softmax do not notice. B (board .hbm vs host .bc) was not recorded. The gate for this model is task_metric.

task_metric.name: wake-word recall, false wake-ups, confusable phrases that fire
task_metric.protocol: Wake words 你好小车 and 小车小车: 202 clips each clean and with MUSAN noise mixed in, 9 synthetic voices. False wake-ups on AISHELL-1 speech, spoken commands and 2.3 h of noisy sessions. 350 confusable phrases (你好小菜, 校车校车, ...). Default threshold 0.25, boost 1.0, 1 trailing blank, 4 active paths. Float = sherpa-onnx KeywordSpotter on the upstream ONNX; int16 = BCDL KeywordSpotter on the board.
task_metric.threshold: recall clean/noisy no lower than float minus ~1 pp, zero false wake-ups, confusables firing no more than float plus ~1 pp
task_metric.measured: float: 96.5% / 87.1% recall, 0 false wake-ups in 4.1 h, confusables 5.4% / 4.6%. int16 BPU: 97.5% / 89.1% recall, 0 false wake-ups in 4.4 h, confusables 5.7% / 4.0%.
task_metric.note: Read the int16 recall as parity with float, not as an improvement over it.

measured.note: S100P, from BCDL's KeywordSpotter on the board.

calibration.shipped: 144 real streaming states: 39 clips (12 wake-word clean, 12 wake-word noisy, 8 confusables, 4 noisy speech at 10 dB, 2 at 0 dB, 1 noise-only), each cut at 20 s; every chunk of the first 8 and every 5th after -> 576 states, every 4th kept.
calibration.time: 15-33 s per state in hb_compile. Shipped build: ~50 min of calibration, 74 min for the whole compile. Rebuild from this recipe: 62 min of calibration, 95 min in all (the host was shared). 576 states would take hours.

rejected_builds.name: softplus as upstream writes it, log(1 + exp(s))
rejected_builds.why: exp(s) spans many orders of magnitude; the Exp quantised to cosine 0 and the whole encoder_out to cosine -0.21 against float. Rewritten to relu(s) + log(1 + exp(-|s|)), the same function with exp in (0, 1].

rejected_builds.name: fbank on samples scaled by 32768
rejected_builds.why: Runtime, not compile: sherpa-onnx feeds samples in [-1, 1]. A port that scaled them agreed with sherpa-onnx on 37 of 87 clips, with nothing in its output looking broken.

rejected_builds.name: cache counter advanced by 4 per chunk
rejected_builds.why: Runtime: processed_lens (now pad_mask) counts at the embedding rate, +8 per 160 ms chunk. Counting the 4 encoder frames runs and drives encoder_out off by up to 34.

graph_rewrites.op: onnxsim with every batch dimension fixed to 1
int64 processed_lens -> float pad_mask [1, 72]; 18 Where(mask, c, x) -> x*(1-m) + c*m; new_processed_lens dropped
graph_rewrites.why: No int64 input and no boolean select on the BPU. Exact for a 0/1 mask.

graph_rewrites.op: Swoosh softplus (34) -> relu(s) + log(1 + exp(-|s|)); 30 inf guards removed
6 relative-position GatherElements (constant indices) -> per-query Slice + Concat on the 4-D tensor, Reshape pair removed
graph_rewrites.why: Each index row is a contiguous run whose offset depends only on the query position.

graph_rewrites.op: 10 depthwise Conv k15 p7 on 1-4 frames -> kernel cropped to the 2L-1 centre taps, pad L-1
graph_rewrites.why: The code generator cannot lower a pad longer than its input ('invalid storage'). Exact: the cropped taps only ever multiply padding zeros.
